identity.name: massing
identity.description: Loads Toronto's 3D Massing shapefile (EPSG:3857, 428,184 records) from CKAN into building_footprints via a class-A guarded upsert (10 columns + geom; the two area columns and geom derived by the geometry validator at INSERT) in one step-scoped transaction.

why_lock.text: Mutual exclusion with every other writer of building_footprints (Spec 47 §A.5 row 56); the shell keeps `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 56;` as a §5.4 source-text constant, asserted equal by src/tests/steps/massing/violations.test.ts.

why.text: Legacy per-batch INSERT verbatim [READ scripts/load-massing.js, anchor `ON CONFLICT (source_id) DO UPDATE SET`]: the legacy five predicates (M-D4 wrong-form, §4.3; widening is F2); area/geom insert_only seeded by the validator (0t/0u) instead of legacy S7/S8; per-1000 batch txn becomes one step txn (M-D11).

on_collision_why.text: M-D3: source_id is md5(geometry) (DBF has no OBJECTID/ID), so identical geometries collide; the file-order last occurrence wins, as legacy's cross-batch overwrite did.

why.text: Only the guarded upsert writes: legacy S1 becomes a declared invariant FAIL, S2/S3 are measured-dead and retired (M-D1), S7/S8 rehome to insert-time derived columns (M-D7).
RLS default-deny on building_footprints (migration 227; 0 policies): the upsert works only under rolbypassrls=true, else it affects 0 rows silently and the verdict still reads PASS.
The GiST index on building_footprints.geom (migrations 065/098) that link_massing's spatial join plans through; without it that join is a sequential scan over ~427K footprints.

on_row_error_why.text: A feature the step refuses to carry is counted and the load continues: a feature with no geometry, or an outer ring with fewer than 4 points, is skipped [READ scripts/load-massing.js, anchor `if (!ring || ring.length < 4)`]. The tolerance is bounded by the declared skip_rate_pct check below; no bare percentage literal survives here (Rule 3).

on_batch_error_why.text: M-D11. The step owns ONE transaction (txn_scope step), so any failed statement rolls back the whole write and fails the step: there is no per-batch boundary left to drop. The legacy per-1000 flush catch that logged, `errors++` and dropped the batch [READ scripts/load-massing.js, anchor `errors++;` in the flush catch] is retired together with the per-batch txn, so `fail_step` is the truthful disposition of a batch failure rather than a retained swallow.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check here reads a counter the library already measured, so a check that throws is a library defect, not an upstream condition — it must redden the run rather than drop its row.

why.text: M-D12. The legacy shell ran `await pool.query('VACUUM ANALYZE building_footprints')` after its geom backfill UPDATE [READ scripts/load-massing.js, anchor `if ((geomUpdateRes.rowCount ?? 0) > 0)`]. That UPDATE is gone — geom and the derived areas are seeded at INSERT — so the vacuum is rehomed as a declared maintenance entry: the executor's runMaintenance (EP-D17) gates it on `building_footprints_dead_tuple_ratio_warn_max` and runs it autocommit, i.e. OUTSIDE the step's write transaction, exactly as VACUUM requires.

Catastrophic-load detector [READ scripts/load-massing.js, `threshold: '>= 400000'`, status WARN — never FAIL]. SEVERITY STAYS WARN: severity is not archetype-derived, and promoting it would introduce a halt that never existed. The bound SHARES the registered variable `sources_building_footprints_floor` (default 400000) with assert_data_bounds through limit_from_config — the SAME key, not a second one (Rule 3, one home per concern). The `limit` string uses verdict.js's R-T addendum `value_min` form (a RAW MEASURED value) and reads the raw rows_read count, NOT `"viol == 0"`: that form plus limit_from_config is the exact AP-D6 trap where resolveLimit substitutes the config value (400000) into the violation form and compares a 0/1 flag against ~400000, so the check would FAIL on every run.

why.text: The legacy INFO audit row `metric: 'records_inserted'` [READ scripts/load-massing.js], carried so the audit table keeps its rows rather than going silent. Purely descriptive (INFO, no negative direction, never gates) and a raw count, so `viol == 0` is the correct limit form here (no limit_from_config).

expect.reports: rows the guarded upsert updated (RETURNING xmax <> 0)

why.text: M-D3: the legacy run reads 4 updated on every unchanged run, from cross-batch self-overwrite of duplicate hashes (source_id is md5(geometry), so identical geometries collide across batch boundaries) [READ scripts/load-massing.js, `ON CONFLICT (source_id) DO UPDATE SET`]. The converted step dedupes the whole file once before writing, so an unchanged rerun reads 0 — the INFO row is carried, its value corrected by construction. Descriptive, no negative direction, `viol == 0` is the raw-count form.

why.text: The legacy INFO row (legacy formula Math.max(0, processed - inserted - updated - skipped)), now the guarded upsert's MEASURED no-op count written.unchanged (Spec 122 §11 KFM 9; scripts/lib/step/conservation.js asserts rows_read = skips + inserted + updated + unchanged). Value moves from the legacy 428,180 to the measured 427,077 on an unchanged run: the 1,107 duplicate-hash rows the legacy absorbed into unchanged are named by duplicate_key_count (M-D3), plus the 4 legacy self-overwrites. expect.reports: source features the step declined to carry (bad_key_count + null_geometry_count + shaped_skipped)

why.text: The runner's skip counter, summing bad_key_count + null_geometry_count + shaped_skipped. The 0s re-bucketing is one-way and declared: a feature with a null geometry now counts as bad_key because coerceKey returns null for it, so the two buckets overlap rather than double-count, and the SUM preserves the legacy `skipped` meaning [READ scripts/load-massing.js, anchor `if (!ring || ring.length < 4)`]. Purely descriptive (INFO, no negative direction gate) — a healthy run shows a counted zero where the legacy could not.

Legacy `status: skipRate >= 5 ? 'FAIL'` [READ scripts/load-massing.js] is a STRICT boundary (5.0% fails) that `pct <=` cannot express, and a `pct` limit on a check that also reports `violations` compares the 0/1 flag (verdict.js `measured` prefers violations) so it could never fail; the compute therefore compares against `ctx.config.massing_skip_rate_max_pct` (Rule 3) and reports violations 0/1. No limit_from_config is declared for the same reason.

The legacy INFO audit row for failed write batches [READ scripts/load-massing.js], carried so the audit table keeps its row rather than going silent. Purely descriptive (INFO, no negative direction, never gates); a raw count, so `viol == 0` is the correct limit form and no limit_from_config is declared.

Legacy `errorRate >= 1 ? 'FAIL'` [READ scripts/load-massing.js] is a STRICT boundary that `pct <=` cannot express, and a `pct` limit on a check that also reports `violations` compares the 0/1 flag (verdict.js `measured` prefers violations) so it could never fail; the compute therefore compares against `ctx.config.massing_batch_error_rate_max_pct` (Rule 3) and reports violations 0/1, so no limit_from_config is declared. Under `txn_scope: \"step\"` a failed batch fails the step before checks run, so a completed run reads 0 (VERIFY-INT-5; address_points precedent). The denominator keeps the legacy per-1000 batch count (execution.batch); the library executor itself chunks statements at pipeline.maxRowsPerInsert(11) = 5957 rows, so the declared batch is the legacy unit, not the executor's.

interrupted_why.text: Rule 12 truthful posture. This step is class A (write_discipline.class "guarded_upsert", retract:"none"): it holds NO retraction path and NO scoped delete, and it writes inside ONE step-scoped transaction (execution.txn_scope:"step"). A kill mid-run therefore leaves exactly what that transaction left — either NOTHING (the txn rolled back, no committed rows) or the FULLY-COMMITTED guarded upsert; there is no half-cleared table an incremental gate could misread as complete, and no retraction to recover because none exists. The force_full_on_next_run obligation binds only targets with retract_when full_only or retract:"all" (per the schema's own note on this field) — neither is declared here. Nothing is owed to a successor run beyond re-running the idempotent upsert, which zero-writes on a byte-identical source (replay:"idempotent_upsert", idempotent_rerun:"zero_writes"). Genuinely none rather than silently ignored.

before_image_why.text: The generic before-image mechanism (scripts/lib/step/write.js writeBeforeImage) mirrors a retraction's write_discipline.scope predicate as a SELECT — it structurally requires a scope to capture. This step declares retract:"none" with write_discipline.scope:"none", so there is no retraction for the mechanism to mirror and nothing to capture. Every column is re-derived from the source on every run, so a re-run recovers the same rows identically without a before-image. Declared out of scope rather than silently skipped (parcels' text shape).

why.text: The guarded upsert committed: every parsed feature is inserted or updated (split by RETURNING xmax = 0), with no retraction (retract:"none"). The step has NO staleness gate (staleness.scope:"none"), so success is the NORMAL terminal of every run — an unchanged source is not a skip, it is a zero-writes completed run.

The declared WARN check tripped with NO FAIL: features_read_floor is WARN-severity and blocking:false, so a load carrying fewer than the configured floor of parsed features still lands and the run is completed_with_warnings — severity stays WARN exactly as the legacy row read, never promoted to a halt.

skip_rate_pct or batch_error_rate_pct reached FAIL — a rising skip rate or a failed write batch (strict legacy boundaries 5% / 1%). The FAIL row is declared; blocking:false, so the run reads as failed and the chain continues (the load already committed, exactly as the legacy loader exited 0).

The CKAN download or the shapefile parse threw before any write was attempted; the temp file is removed on this path as on every other, and building_footprints is untouched (no transaction was opened).
inputs.expect_nonempty is true: a source that parses to ZERO records fails rather than landing an empty 'success' — an empty shapefile is a publisher error, not an empty load.

Advisory lock 56 is held by another process. Pre-conversion the step wrapped everything in pipeline.withAdvisoryLock and returned silently when the lock was not acquired (legacy `if (!lockResult.acquired) return;`); the library now emits a row-derived SKIP summary instead of a silent return.
